rule: Stagger is a flinch by default. A hit becomes a knockdown only when the raw health damage (before armour) is above zero and at least agility times the knockdown damage multiplier, AND an odds roll from 0 to 99 meets a threshold that rises with agility. Otherwise it is a flinch (hit recovery). A knockdown lasts exactly as long as its hit animation: the state clears when that animation stops playing. Statuses are keyed by (effect id, argument); magnitudes with the same key add. A non-stackable spell from the same source does not re-add while active; a temporary clashing effect replaces the old one. Consumables are temporary AND stackable so they add. Each frame's application is clipped to the time left (min(timeLeft, dt)). Corprus-style statuses worsen every 24 game hours. Fear-like statuses are AI-setting modifiers (Demoralize and Rally on Flee, Frenzy and Calm on Fight), valid only on NPCs of the matching kind; the player is never a valid target.

keep: Flinch by default; fall only when a damage gate and an agility-scaled roll both pass.
A knockdown lasts exactly as long as its clip; the clip length is the duration.
One ledger key per (effect, argument); magnitudes with the same key add.
Spells refresh rather than re-stack; consumables add.
Each frame's application is clipped to the time left, so the last frame does not overshoot.
Knocked-down and paralysed states remove evasion and block, and turn hand-to-hand hits into health damage.
Fear-like effects are AI-setting modifiers on the Flee and Fight settings, valid only on NPCs of the matching kind.
A killing blow while knocked down plays its own death-on-the-ground clip.
change: Stagger roll comes from the server seed and is written to the fight record, not math.random in a client Lua script.
Duration stored in server ticks; the client plays the clip at that rate, so the server tick is not tied to the animation.
Per-target knockdown cooldown in the engine, because three attackers roll three times per round.
Round the per-frame status magnitude in float and apply once per status change (open check: whether the donor's Frenzy and Calm flags make this matter).
Use our own numbers, names and poses; no donor magnitudes or clip names.
look_test: Training dummy in the Pit with light, medium and heavy hit buttons. Light: flinch only. Heavy on a low-agility dummy: fall, grounded for the clip, then stand-up. Heavy on a high-agility dummy: flinch only. Death while down: a separate ground death clip. Judge on a 375-wide screen that flinch and fall differ at a glance and the fall ends where its clip ends.
